passages_note: Distinct (pdf_page_index, quote) groups: 14, covering all 21 listed records. Method: opened each stated PDF page as an image and compared with pdftotext -raw output of the same page (read-only, nothing written) to confirm exact characters.
summary_notes: Every quote is on its stated page; none needed a nearby page.

No quote matches the page word for word. In every case the difference is one to four words: an omitted or added word, a corrected or uncorrected typo in the book, or a changed preposition. The sentence in each record is the right sentence.
Only one record is wrong in substance: ch01 record 6 (Gd3+ labelled mGlu1 Receptor Agonist; the page calls Gd3+ a potentiator).

Five records are supported only with a caveat (see substance_caveat): ch23 r5 (hypothesis only), ch24 r2 (page says partial agonist of NOS), ch27 r9 (indirect effect on active RhoA), ch29 r31 and r32 (page says 'regulate the activation of HSL', suppression of FFA release is the stated outcome).

passages.quote: in the presence of an antagonist or in the presence of a potentiator
passages.page_wording: mGlu1 structures obtained in the presence of an antagonist (MCPG) or in the presence of a potentiator (Gd3+) in which the dimer orientation is R and A, respectively (Tsuchiya et al., 2002)
passages.why_extraction_missed_it: The record quote leaves out the parenthetical '(MCPG)' between 'antagonist' and 'or' without marking the gap, and the sentence wraps across a line break ('presence of an / antagonist'). The text layer contains the sentence intact.
passages.substance_reasoning: The page says Gd3+ is a potentiator (a positive allosteric modulator) of mGlu1, used to obtain the active (A) dimer structure; it does not call Gd3+ an agonist, so the mechanism name 'mGlu1 Receptor Agonist' is not supported. 'mGlu1 Receptor Positive Allosteric Modulator/Potentiator' is what the page supports.

passages.quote: VU0155041 is an allosteric agonist and positive allosteric modulator with potency nearly 10-fold that of PHCCC
passages.page_wording: VU0155041 is an allosteric agonist and positive allosteric modulator with potency nearly 10-fold of that of PHCCC, moreover, VU0155041 concentration-dependently diminished haloperidol-induced catalepsy and reversed reserpine-mediated akinesia in mice
passages.why_extraction_missed_it: Transcription slip: the book reads 'nearly 10-fold of that of PHCCC' and the record dropped the word 'of'. The sentence also wraps across a line break after 'positive allosteric'.
passages.substance_reasoning: The page states VU0155041 is an allosteric agonist and PAM of mGlu4 (the preceding sentence introduces it as a 'more recent PAM of mGlu4'), which supports 'mGlu4 Receptor Agonist'.

passages.quote: among these there are the baclofen derivatives, saclofen and 2-OH saclofen; CGP54626, the most common of the antagonists; and CGP71872
passages.page_wording: The number of antagonists is much greater than that of agonists, among these ligands there are the baclofen derivatives, saclofen and 2-OH saclofen; CGP54626, the most common of the antagonists; and CGP71872; the former two possessing high micromolar affinity, whilst the latter two exhibit low nanomolar affinity (Kaupmann et al., 1997).
passages.why_extraction_missed_it: Transcription slip: the record has 'among these there are' where the book has 'among these ligands there are'. In addition '2-OH saclofen' is split by a line-end hyphen ('2-' / 'OH saclofen') in the text layer.
passages.substance_reasoning: All four named compounds (saclofen, 2-OH saclofen, CGP54626, CGP71872) are listed as antagonists, in the GABAB discussion (Fig. 5 on the same page is GABAB agonists). The sentence follows a remark about a GABAC antagonist, but the list itself is under the GABAB section, so 'GABAB Receptor Antagonist' is supported for each drug.

passages.quote: Even in the presence of μ agonist DAMGO (100 nM) and δ agonist DPDPE (200 nM)
passages.page_wording: Even in the presence of μ agonist DAMDO (100 nM) and δ agonist DPDPE (200 nM), the Kd and Bmax values for [3H]TRK-820 did not change (Kd = 0.51±0.03 nM, Bmax = 265±27.2 fmol/mg protein) (Endoh et al., 2000).
passages.why_extraction_missed_it: Two causes visible in the text layer: the book prints the typo 'DAMDO' (the record has the intended 'DAMGO'), and the Greek letters μ and δ are stored as symbol-font private-use characters, not as ordinary U+03BC / U+03B4, so a string match fails even where the words agree.
passages.substance_reasoning: The page labels DAMDO (i.e. DAMGO) a μ agonist and DPDPE a δ agonist, matching 'Opioid Mu Receptor Agonist' and 'Opioid Delta Receptor Agonist'. Note the sentence is about the agonists being used as tools in a TRK-820 binding experiment, but the receptor-subtype labels are stated plainly.

passages.quote: the observed pharmacological effects could be attributed to a potential antagonism with glutamate receptors and/or inhibition of noradrenalin-dopamine releasing
passages.page_wording: Taking into consideration the structural similarity, grosso modo,(molecular modeling are underway and are unpublished results yet) between secondary metabolites, DHAA, related derivatives and cannabinoids, the observed pharmacological effects could be attribute to a potential antagonism with glutamate receptors and/or inhibition of noradrenalin-dopamine releasing.

passages.substance_reasoning: The page does name glutamate-receptor antagonism for DHAA and related derivatives, but only as a possibility ('could be', 'potential'), inferred from structural similarity with cannabinoids, with the modelling stated to be unpublished. If the record presents it as an established mechanism, it overstates the page.

passages.quote: CO has been shown to serve as a partial agonist of nitric oxide synthetase (NOS) and thus, may down-regulate the level of NOS-dependent signaling
passages.page_wording: CO has been shown to serve as a partial agonist to nitric oxide synthetase (NOS) and thus, may down-regulate the level of NOS-dependent signaling (Hangai-Hoger et al., 2007; Ishikawa et al., 2005).
passages.why_extraction_missed_it: Transcription slip: the book says 'partial agonist to', the record says 'partial agonist of'. In addition the sentence wraps across lines at 'partial / agonist' and 'NOS- / dependent', which breaks a single-line search.
passages.substance_caveat: The page says 'partial agonist' of NOS, not inhibitor.
passages.substance_reasoning: The net effect stated is down-regulation of NOS-dependent signaling, which is consistent with the label 'Nitric Oxide Synthase Inhibitor' as a functional summary, but the page's own term is 'partial agonist'. The label is an interpretation.

passages.page_wording: Ethanol reduced endogenous levels of acive RhoA due to an increase in the activity of small Rho GTP-ases, reduced phosphoinositides levels and induced changes in the dynamics and organization of the actin cytoskeleton.

passages.substance_reasoning: The page says ethanol lowers the level of active RhoA, which supports a functional 'RhoA Inhibitor' label. It does not say ethanol binds or inhibits RhoA directly, and attributes the drop to increased activity of small Rho GTPases (wording as printed).

passages.quote: complex of AMD3100 has a 10-fold higher affinity to the receptor as compared to AMD3100 alone
passages.page_wording: Thus, the Zn2+ complex of AMD3100 binds with a 10-fold higher affinity to the receptor as compared to AMD3100 alone and has an up to 6-fold increased potency as an anti-HIV agent.

passages.substance_reasoning: The page calls AMD3100 'a CXCR4 receptor inhibitor' and 'a symmetrical nonpeptide antagonist' of the CXCR4 chemokine receptor, and says the Zn2+ complex binds the receptor with higher affinity and is more potent, which supports 'CXCR4 Receptor Antagonist' for the complex.

passages.quote: The pharmacological effects of NSAIDs stem from the inhibition of enzymes in the cyclooxygenase family (COX).
passages.page_wording: Aspirin (acetylsalicylic acid) belongs to the family of nonsteroidal antirheumatics (NSAR), which have anti-inflammatory and pain-relieving effects The pharmacological effects of NSARs stem from the inhibition of enzymes in the cyclooxygenase family (COX).

passages.substance_reasoning: The page states NSAR effects stem from inhibition of cyclooxygenase (COX) enzymes, supporting 'Cyclooxygenase Inhibitor'. Note the record's drug label expands to 'nonsteroidal antiinflammatory drugs' while the page says 'nonsteroidal antirheumatics'.

passages.quote: regulate the activation of HSL (hormone-sensitive lipase), resulting in suppression of free fatty acid release
passages.page_wording: VO(alx)2 regulates the activation of the FoxO1, while Zn(alx)2 and Zn(tanm)2 regulate the activation of HSL (hormone-sensitive lipase), resulting in the suppression of free fatty acid release.
passages.why_extraction_missed_it: Transcription slip: the record omits the word 'the' before 'suppression'. The sentence also wraps across several lines.

passages.substance_reasoning: The page says both zinc complexes regulate HSL activation with the result that free fatty acid release is suppressed, and earlier says they inhibited epinephrine-induced FFA release. That is consistent with HSL inhibition, but the page never says the complexes inhibit HSL directly; 'Hormone-Sensitive Lipase Inhibitor' is an inference from the net effect.
